articles.title: Is Diego Lopes a BMF?
articles.description: New DraftKings Customers turn five bucks into one hundred and fifty in total bonuses, paid over 14 days. The Crown Is Yours! Sign up using https://dkng.co/sonnen or through my promo code SONNEN. #DKPartner Chael Sonnen just drew a line the UFC will not like: Diego Lopes is not a BMF. He has fought for championships, sure, but BMF status comes with veteran status, and Lopes has not been around long enough. That caught even the room off guard. Here is Chael's thesis. The BMF belt is not supposed to be linear. It is a one-off belt, so stop worrying about passing it on to someone else (0:28). It does not have to happen once a year or once a month. Let it be super special. Let it happen only between two guys who are truly deserving. If you turn it into just another title, it means nothing, like a fake Olympic medal presented at a local tournament, same metal, no meaning (1:16). Chael likes the idea of a lineage, but admits there is nothing he can do about that now. So build it up instead. Have the media talk about it. Have Joe Rogan call some guy the next BMF, then let it happen eight months later (2:19). That is how you make it different and unique. And he points to the blueprint: Nate Diaz vs Jorge Masvidal, two guys with rough records who were never champions and never would be, and the Rock walked into Madison Square Garden and wrapped the belt around the winner's waist (3:07). That is what the BMF is supposed to be. Do not kill it by making it a regular belt. articles.title: Rakhmonov vs Morales is Next?
articles.description: Shavkat Rakhmonov just dropped a TikTok hint that says everything without naming a name: he wants to put his 19-0 record against another undefeated record. Do the math and there's exactly one guy that fits: Michael Morales, 19-0. Chael breaks down the Rakhmonov callout that isn't technically a callout, and asks the question the comments are already fighting about: is Rakhmonov vs Morales next, and is that actually a great fight? Then the plot thickens. Morales put out a callout video naming every name in the welterweight division, and Chael says the video should have been 25 seconds long. Meanwhile Rakhmonov isn't calling for Islam Makhachev, Morales has open challenges to Islam, Ian Garry, and Rakhmonov, and somehow the one guy who gets the direct line to Islam is Carlos Prates, the man nobody asked to the dance. articles.title: If Talbott Gets a Title Shot, O’Malley Should Too #ufc
articles.description: Sean O’Malley vs. Michael “Venom” Page? No. 1 contender fight? articles.title: Chael's Problem with Michael Morales' Promo Video
articles.description: Michael Morales dropped a slick, self-produced promo video, and Chael Sonnen has notes, plus a prediction about what comes next. Chael starts with full credit: the production is top-shelf. Lighting, sound, Morales looking sharp in a suit, a fight-promo feel with real clips. Then he tackles it two ways. First, the production: Morales speaks another language and the music is mixed so loud it's hard to understand him. Chael's fix is simple, turn the music down and let the fighter be heard. Second, the script: Morales said too much and named too many names. Chael's rule is say a third of what you planned. One clear callout, then stop. Then Chael gets into the philosophy. The chicken-and-egg of stardom: you can't become a star without a media push, so how do you get the push? Kevin Lee, Colby Covington, and Henry Cejudo solved it by taking the financial risk and building their own promotional machines. Chael loves that Morales did the same. And the fallout is already here. Shavkat Rakhmonov answered with a TikTok caption hinting at 19-0 versus 19-0, Morales versus Rakhmonov is suddenly very real, and there's a quiet race with Carlos Prates to be next for Islam Makhachev. Chael lays out how the title-race game gets played in the media and by managers, and asks the only question that matters: which fight do you want to see? articles.title: Daniel Cormier REACTS to INSANE KNOCKOUTS from Talbott, Ribovics vs Green, & Pinas, Silva beats Wang
articles.description: UFC 332 from Salt Lake City, Utah was both INSANE and HISTORIC, featuring a UFC-record 11 knockouts, nine of which came in the first round! Natalia Silva headlined the card against Wang "Joker" Cong, winning via unanimous decision. DC looks back at every knockout from the night, and breaks down his favorites, including Payton Talbott finishing former champ Deiveson Figueiredo, Esteban Ribovics's first-round finish of King Green, and incredible knockouts from Imanol Rodriguez, Damian Pinas, Jacobe Smith, Anthony Wint, Johnny Walker and so many more! Plus don't miss what Cormier thinks is next for Natalia Silva, and if there is anyone who can challenge her for the belt right now aside from Valentina Shevchenko.
